name: Sarcomere
desc: Striated muscle at the ultrastructure -- the sarcomere. Myofibrils stack across the frame, each a run of repeating contractile units read as the classic electron-micrograph banding: dark Z-lines bounding every sarcomere, light I-bands of thin actin, the dark A-band of myosin overlap with its lighter H-zone and central M-line. The muscle works: an activation wave travels along the fibres on incommensurate rates, so the sliding-filament mechanism plays out -- Z-lines pull together and the I-bands and H-zone narrow while the A-band holds its width -- a perpetual contraction and relaxation that ripples along the fibre and never re-phases. Offered as a grey transmission electron micrograph, polarised-light birefringence, Z-disc immunofluorescence, or a false-colour tension map.

scale.doc: magnification - sarcomeres grow, fewer larger bands, guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: contraction rate and how fast the activation wave travels

density.doc: number of stacked myofibrils and wave crest count

contract.doc: contraction depth - how far the Z-lines pull together and the I-bands narrow

hue.doc: base hue of the banding / labels

style.doc: aesthetic: grey transmission electron micrograph / polarised-light birefringence with glowing A-bands / Z-disc immunofluorescence / false-colour tension map
